title: Dafiment Bank Pyramid Scheme Collapses, Wiping Out Serbian Depositors

Multiple independent sources corroborate the core facts: Dafina Milanović's Dafiment Bank was registered/founded in October 1991 (nova.rs), operated with tacit backing/origination by Slobodan Milošević's government (IWPR: "set up by Milanovic with the help of the authorities"; Vreme: "Milošević invented Dafiment Bank," with a vice-governor tasked to operationalize it), and paid extraordinarily high interest rates during hyperinflation and wartime sanctions (IWPR cites 11-15% for hard currency and 75-195% for dinar accounts; other Serbian sources cite different but similarly extreme figures — the specific "45% a month" figure in the event isn't verbatim in any single source but is well within the documented range of rates offered over the bank's life). The bank restricted withdrawals amid a depositor run beginning spring 1993 (Washington Post, dated April 2, 1993: "Serb Banks Face Run by Depositors") and collapsed by mid-1993 (bankruptcy dated May 1, 1993 per Serbian press; Milanović attempted to flee July 14, 1993). Multiple sources converge on ~150 million marks owed to depositors at shutdown (IWPR/aggregated summary: "when it shut down, it owed its depositors about 150 million [marks]"), consistent with "tens of thousands" to ~150,000 depositors, many pensioners, losing life savings. The near-simultaneous collapse of the second pyramid bank Jugoskandik (Jezdimir Vasiljević fled March 7, 1993) is independently confirmed via Wikipedia/Grokipedia summary of Vasiljević, describing the two collapses as a compounded "disastrous blow to the Serbian economy." All core elements — country (Serbia), year (1993), actor, mechanism, government backing, scale, and the compounding Jugoskandik collapse — check out materially as described.
